map.塑料成型收缩率计算 使用指南: Plastic Moulding Shrinkage Rate Calculator User Guide
map.输入塑料的型腔尺寸与实测制品尺寸，工具计算成型收缩率；也可反向由目标收缩率推算模: Enter the cavity dimensions and the measured part dimensions and the tool computes the moulding shrinkage; it can also work backwards from a target shrinkage rate to the cavity oversizing needed, covering shrinkage compensation design for injection moulding, blow moulding, and other common processes.
map.模具设计时，用收缩率=(模具尺寸−制品尺寸)/模具尺寸×100% 反推制品实际收: In mould design, the shrinkage rate =(mould size − product size)/mould size×100% gives the actual shrinkage of the product and the shrinkage ratio.
map.模腔放缩时，用 模具尺寸=目标尺寸÷(1−收缩率) 放大模腔，保证出模冷却后制品: When scaling the cavity, enlarge it with mould size = target size ÷ (1 − shrinkage rate) so the part meets its dimensions after cooling in the mould.
map.试模修正时，按首件实测收缩微调模腔，补偿材料各向异性与工艺波动。: When correcting after the trial mould, fine-tune the cavity using the shrinkage measured on the first piece to compensate for material anisotropy and process variation.
map.收缩率与模腔放缩示例: Shrinkage rate and cavity scaling example
map.：模具 100 mm、制品 98 mm → 收缩率 = (100−98)/100: : With a mould of 100 mm and a part of 98 mm → shrinkage = (100−98)/100×100% = 2.0%, a shrinkage of 2.0 mm and a ratio of about 1:50. For a target part of 98 mm at 2% shrinkage the cavity should be opened to 98÷(1−0.02) = 100.0 mm, an increase of 2.0 mm. If the trial measures only 99.4 mm (0.6 mm shrinkage) the cavity must be enlarged accordingly.
map.流动方向分子取向使纵向与横向收缩不同，玻纤增强料更明显（纤维限制取向方向收缩）。: Molecular orientation in the flow direction makes longitudinal and transverse shrinkage differ, which is more obvious in glass fibre reinforced material (the fibres restrain shrinkage along the orientation direction). Design should take the midpoint of the material's standard shrinkage and leave margin per flow direction.
map.模腔放大量怎么校核？: How Do You Check the Cavity Oversizing?
map.按目标尺寸÷(1−收缩率) 放大，再结合试模实测收缩率回代微调；高收缩或易变形件: Scale up by target size ÷ (1 − shrinkage rate), then fine-tune using the shrinkage measured from a trial mould; for high shrinkage or easily distorted parts leave trimming margin rather than over-scaling in one go.
